name: settings-search-finds-a-row
description: The settings search field sits above the rail (settings.js's renderSettings) and reaches into PANE_ROWS, not just the nine pane titles. A query lands on a result list under the field rather than a filtered rail, so the rail's roving tabindex keeps working while the field holds text. Choosing a result switches pane and marks the row. Escape clears the field before it does anything to the window - typed here for real through CDP, not a synthetic dispatchEvent, since that is the one behaviour the node suite cannot exercise (its keydown is dispatched by the test itself, never a trusted event).

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
Atrium MUST be frontmost or cmd+comma opens Finder Settings instead
open Settings; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
window opens on General - renderSettings(root, PANES[0].id)
The field's own column, ahead of the rail - kids[0] is the window's drag strip, above both

actions.expression: (() => { const f = document.querySelector('.settings-search-field'); f.focus(); f.value = 'glass opacity'; f.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); return document.querySelectorAll('.settings-search-result').length; })()
actions.note: A row on the Appearance pane, found from the General pane the window opened on
the result list under the field, General still the rail's own selection
Choosing the result switches the pane
renderSettings() rebuilds the tree synchronously - slack for the ssh/eval round trip
Evidence: Appearance on screen with the chosen row briefly lit
The row itself carries the mark, not just the pane switch
the query is untouched by choosing a result - only Escape clears it

actions.expression: (() => { const items = [...document.querySelectorAll('.settings-rail-item')]; return items.length + ':' + items.filter((i) => i.tabIndex === 0).length; })()
actions.note: Every rail item still rendered, and the roving tabindex still names exactly one of them the Tab stop, with the field holding text

actions.expression: (() => { const f = document.querySelector('.settings-search-field'); f.value = ''; f.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); f.focus(); return document.activeElement === f; })()
actions.note: a clean field, refocused, ahead of the real keystrokes below
confirms the CDP keystrokes actually landed in the field before Escape is measured against them
THE MEASUREMENT - a real, trusted keydown, not a scenario-side dispatchEvent

assertions.note: the browser window AND the settings window - Escape must not have closed it

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q still quits with the settings window open
